newsitem.title: USA: Calif. judge approves AOL settlement.
newsitem.headline: Calif. judge approves AOL settlement.

text.p: A California judge has approved a modified settlement in a class-action lawsuit against American Online Inc (AOL), the San Francisco Chronicle reported on Saturday.

It said San Francisco Superior Court Judge James Robertson approved the settlement on Friday between the online service and disgruntled customers. It said the new settlement, which modifies terms of a two-month-old tentative settlement, was a modestly improved deal for consumers.
Under the new agreement, AOL will give users who spent more than $300 on the service from July 1991 to March 1996 an additional hour of usage for each $300 in charges.
People who qualify but are no longer customers of AOL will share in a fund worth up to $700,000. A formal ruling is expected next month, it said.
The agreement settles 11 suits that were consolidated into a class action lawsuit in San Francisco on behalf of millions of AOL subscribers.

The plaintiffs alleged that AOL rounded up charges to the next minute without telling them, added another minute and 15 seconds for any online session over 45 minutes and that it charged customers for time spent in designated "free" areas online.

A tentative settlement reached in July would have given millions of AOL subscribers one free hour of online use. Plaintiffs in 10 of the suits agreed to the initial settlement but one plaintiff objected, saying heavy users would not get enough free hours under the initial settlement. The objection forced Friday's court hearing.
AOL officials could not immediately be reached for comment. The Chronicle quoted AOL spokeswoman Pam McGraw as saying that the "best thing to do is settle and move forward."
